genre_name: Trial-level surrogate endpoint evaluation (meta-analytic surrogacy: R2 trial, R2 individual, surrogate threshold effect)
scope: Meta-analyses that test whether treatment effects on a candidate surrogate (PFS, PFS2, RFS/DFS, ORR, pCR, MRD, proteinuria, LDL-C, patient-reported scores...) predict treatment effects on the final endpoint (OS, kidney failure, cardiovascular events) across randomised trials. Covers aggregate-data systematic reviews with weighted trial-level regression (6/9 exemplars) and IPD two-level designs (copula or Bayesian individual- plus trial-level; 3/9). Outputs: R2 trial (with CI), individual- or arm-level association, STE, leave-one-out or external validation, subgroup/sensitivity analyses. Excludes single-trial mediation or proportion-explained analyses, prognostic-marker association studies without randomised contrasts, and reviews of surrogacy methods. Oncology dominates (6/9); non-oncology exemplars: cardiometabolic (E7), nephrology (E8), heart failure (E9).
word_count_convention: jats_structure.py prose words; captions/tables/citations/headings excluded; main = I+M+R+D(+L,C)

checklists.name: ReSEEM (Reporting of Surrogate Endpoint Evaluation using Meta-analyses)
checklists.citation: Xie W, Halabi S, Tierney JF, et al. A systematic review and recommendation for reporting of surrogate endpoint evaluation using meta-analyses. JNCI Cancer Spectr. 2019;3(1):pkz002
checklists.frequency: 3/9 cite it (E2, E4, E6); 1/9 states adherence (E4)
checklists.notes: The genre's dedicated guideline: 28 items. Items 5-13 and 17-19 defer to PRISMA / PRISMA-IPD; genre-specific items: 14 endpoint definitions, 15 surrogacy criteria, 16A-E individual-level, aggregate and trial-level models, STE, validation and sensitivity, 20-21 per-trial characteristics and effect estimates, 22 bubble plot with regression line and prediction interval plus STE, 23 validation, 26 limitations at several levels. Published 2019 (PMC6649812); no 2024 update was found.

standard_items.text: Aggregate trial-level data only: individual-level surrogacy and within-trial mediation cannot be assessed; or, for IPD designs, IPD from only a subset of trials or one sponsor
Small number of trials/comparisons gives imprecise R2 and wide prediction intervals; phase 2 trials widen effect CIs
Heterogeneity in populations, regimens, tumour types or settings pooled in one regression
Immature final-endpoint data or short follow-up at the data cut; effects may change with longer follow-up
Surrogacy may not transfer to new drug classes, mechanisms, lines or settings
Surrogate definitions, assessment timing or instrument domains differ across trials
Crossover and post-progression therapy dilute effects on the final endpoint
Risk of bias in included trials (open-label, incomplete outcome data)
Incomplete trial capture or publication bias; reliance on published, not raw, data

variation_notes: Data type drives the most structure. Aggregate-data reviews (E1, E2, E4, E6, E7, E9) carry PRISMA machinery (registration, search subsection, flow diagram, risk of bias) and report arm-level rather than individual-level association. IPD papers (E3, E5, E8) drop the flow diagram and registration, add copula or Bayesian models and Kaplan-Meier figures by surrogate status, and run longer Methods (E5: 1300 words). Venue sets the abstract headings and summary box (JAMA 8-heading abstract plus Key Points; Lancet-family Interpretation/Funding headings plus Research in context; JCO Context box; BMJ-family 'What this study adds'), the separate Conclusions section (4/9), and back-matter placement. Reference counts vary with venue rather than design (27-73, plus one outlier at 190 in E2). Interpretation thresholds are not standard: ReSEEM-style R2 bands (E2, E6), IQWiG CI-bound rule on r (E3, E4, E7), or ad hoc bands (E5). STE appears in only 2/9 despite ReSEEM recommending it.
lint_notes: The surrogacy scatter is mandatory: one point per trial/comparison, bubble area proportional to weight (sample size, deaths or inverse variance), log-scale effects, weighted regression line; flag a missing 95% prediction band (ReSEEM item 22; shown in only 3/9) and, if an STE is reported, require it marked on the plot.
Every R2 trial needs a 95% CI and the number of trials/comparisons it rests on, in both the abstract and the Results.
Require prespecified surrogacy thresholds in Methods (cite ReSEEM R2 bands or the IQWiG CI-bound rule) and a Results strength label that uses the same scale.
Require the weighting scheme and the unit of analysis (trial vs comparison; multi-arm trials split or down-weighted) to be stated.

Aggregate-data designs: require PRISMA flow, registration (or 'not registered'), search strategy in the supplement and a risk-of-bias assessment. IPD designs: require trial provenance, ethics/consent statement and the individual-level method (copula/Kendall tau/Spearman or Bayesian).
A limitations paragraph must name the data level (trial-level only, or partial IPD), the number of trials, and endpoint maturity; some also note class or setting specificity (3/9).
Do not accept 'surrogate validated' wording when R2 < 0.7 or the IQWiG lower CI bound is < 0.85; the abstract verdict must match the prespecified criteria.
Per-trial effect estimates (both endpoints) must appear in a table or supplement so the regression is reproducible (ReSEEM item 21).
Spelled-out numbers start abstract Results sentences ('Eighteen RCTs...'); trial-count regexes must accept words as well as digits.
notes: ReSEEM is Xie et al. 2019 (JNCI Cancer Spectr 3(1):pkz002); no 2024 revision was found. CONSORT-Surrogate and SPIRIT-Surrogate (BMJ 2024) cover trials that use surrogates; no exemplar cites them, correctly.

Candidate pool was thin for non-oncology in 2022-2026 OA full text: the CKD-EPI CT GFR-slope (Nat Med 2023) and albuminuria (Nat Med 2026) meta-analyses are not available as Europe PMC XML (author manuscript or not in PMC), so they were not used.
E7 is labelled 'Review' by its journal (umbrella review feeding an original trial-level surrogacy regression). It was kept as a cardiometabolic exemplar; its abstract is unstructured in the JATS.
E6's Discussion cites a prior pancreatic-cancer surrogacy meta-analysis once; title, abstract and keywords are clean, so the contamination rule holds.
Competing-interests (E5) and funding (E1) statements may exist on publisher pages but are absent from the JATS; frequencies count JATS only.
Only E7 shares analysis code (OSF), so code_availability is not listed as a section (1/9).
New display-item ids (not in the shared vocabulary): arm_level_scatter (display item); loo_cross_validation_plot appears only in E6's measured kinds (a leave-one-out observed-vs-predicted plot).
Limitations word counts for E4, E5 and E8 are estimates read from the Discussion paragraph structure; the others are the measured paragraph lengths.
